brief.headline: Offer to pay in 15 days instead of 30 in exchange for a 6% price cut — their cash is stuck for 101 days, so early payment is worth about 12% a year to them.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 6% price cut if we pay in 15 days instead of 30.
priceAsk.target: A 6% reduction (roughly half their 12.16% borrowing cost for the 15-day advance).
priceAsk.basis: Their cash is stuck for 101 days versus 64 days at similar firms — cash is tight for them. They borrow money at about 12.16%, so paying 15 days early is worth roughly that rate to them. Our current price sits at the top of the fair market band (₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg), so a 6% cut keeps them in the fair zone while we share the benefit of freeing their cash.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days (instead of the current 30 days) in exchange for the 6% price cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster costs us ₹26.60 L in cash, but the 6% discount should more than cover that over the year.

brief.financialLeverage: They keep only 2.3% of every ₹100 they sell as profit, so there's very little room for a big price squeeze. But their cash is stuck for 101 days — much longer than similar firms at 64 days — and they owe a lot (1.25× their own cash, totalling ₹282.62 Cr). They borrow at about 12.16%, so early payment is real money to them. We're a tiny customer (0.61% of their ₹1064.86 Cr revenue), so we can't bully them, but we can trade cash-flow help for a fair price cut. Push the payment-for-discount swap hard; avoid a pure price fight that could hurt a fragile supplier.

evidence.point: Their cash is stuck much longer than similar firms
They borrow money at a high rate
They owe a lot relative to their own cash
We're a small customer to them
Our current laminate price sits at the top of the fair market band
evidence.figure: ₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg — verdict: MARKET-FAIR (top of fair band)

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter, already a tiny FDC supplier — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets (₹2755.75 Cr revenue, health C 58/100).

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant that makes both the film substrate and does conversion — can second-source at scale (₹16492.00 Cr revenue, health C 46/100).

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of the global Constantia group, specialises in pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong second-source option (₹222.04 Cr revenue, health D 31/100).

risks: They're in the 'grey zone' financially (Altman Z-score 2.36) and have EPF payment delays — keep an eye on supply security and don't push so hard you tip them over.
Their credit rating is middling (CARE BBB+ / Stable) — spread risk by qualifying a second converter now.
We're only 0.61% of their revenue, so we have limited clout — frame the ask as a win-win (we help their cash flow, they help our cost) rather than a hard squeeze.
Paying 15 days earlier costs us ₹26.60 L in cash — make sure the 6% saving pays back that investment over the year and get finance sign-off before committing.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to help free up your cash by paying in 15 days instead of 30 — in return, we're looking for a 6% price reduction that shares the benefit with us.
